turns.query: Using Apple's fiscal-2025 SEC Notes dataset facts with month-end-rounded period date 2025-09-30, build the undiscounted long-term-debt principal maturity ladder from the six separately tagged buckets: next twelve months, years two through five, and after year five. Report each bucket and their sum. Reconcile that sum to the reported consolidated gross long-term-debt carrying amount: report the number of all physical rows for that measure/date/unit, the number of physical rows carrying no dimensions, the number of distinct numeric values among those no-dimension rows, the consolidated gross-debt amount, and maturity sum minus gross debt. Interpret the reconciliation and row-count evidence.

Extend the turn-1 ladder with the six undimensioned unrecorded unconditional purchase-obligation buckets for the same end date: years one through five and after year five. Report each bucket, their sum, combined debt-plus-purchase commitments due in year one, and combined undiscounted commitments across all six timing buckets. Explain the accounting boundary between the two ladders.

Now apply the following present-value convention to the two turn-2 ladders. Use the latest reported Treasury par-yield-curve observation on or before 2025-09-30 and its 5-year par yield as one flat annual discount rate. Treat years one through five as end-of-year cash flows at t=1,...,5 and the after-year-five bucket as one payment at t=10. Report the curve date and yield, and the base present value of the debt ladder, purchase ladder and combined ladder. Explain what this construction can and cannot measure.

Shock the turn-3 flat discount rate upward by exactly 100 basis points, holding every disclosed cash-flow bucket and timing convention fixed. Report the shocked rate; shocked debt, purchase and combined present values; and the combined percentage change relative to the base combined present value. Interpret the sign and distinguish the modeled present-value change from contractual nominal payments.
